# Native exact-face selection controls

Original OOXML generated by `tools/native_face_selection_fixture.py`; no corpus
content or font binaries are included. The reference application opened the exact
source read-only and produced `native.pdf`. The reference extractor records native
character-origin advances and source/PDF hashes.

Sixteen rows cover regular, bold, italic and bold italic in Franklin Gothic
Medium, Franklin Gothic Demi, Arial and Times New Roman. On this Windows host,
CSS's Franklin Gothic Medium selects a face whose sample advance equals the
installed Demi face; `local("Franklin Gothic Medium")` selects the requested
Medium face. Demi also needs its installed italic companion when registered as
an exact face. The reference application's reference distinguishes these cases without hard-coding a
font-family exception in the engine.

Browser checks compare the first-to-last character origins within 0.25pt across
all sixteen styles, and verify editing, original font declarations, unrelated
package parts, export/reopen and exact undo. Existing synthetic-bold ink controls
are checked separately. ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.2.26 (`rFonts`), 17.3.2.1
(`b`) and 17.3.2.16 (`i`) describe the retained declarations. This fixes host CSS
face selection; no reference/spec contradiction is asserted.

The existing reviewed-family test's six-versus-three request assertion and
Source Sans Light's 45.6226776pt position error reproduce with the unchanged
font-availability module. They remain open; neither tolerance was loosened.
The existing Open Sans expected-failure shaping oracle also remains.
